methodologyNote: Many-to-one (inbound: arrive by target, latest possible departure). Same router as Liverpool (midnight-wrap fix, inf-averaging fix). 1937 feed is a real digitised timetable (not synthetic/assumed like Manchester's), trams only -- no historical buses, unlike Liverpool's 1937 feed which included both. As supplied, every route had only 2 stops (city + destination, nothing between) -- corrected by adding stops along the real surveyed KMZ track alignment between them, timed with an accel/decel/dwell model solved to reproduce each route's own real scheduled time exactly (so end-to-end time is unchanged, only the previously-missing stop-by-stop detail is added). The supplied destination points were geocoded place names, 21 of 22 off the track by up to 1.4 km; each route now ends at its surveyed KMZ branch end (e.g. Crookes at Heavygate Road), with every scheduled total kept. Modern feed is GB rail + England bus (DfT BODS), filtered to a 30 km radius, including Supertram's four lines (Blue, Yellow, Purple, Tram Train) as registered in BODS. Transfer penalty 5 min per change (the low end of published interchange valuations, about 5-18 min; sensitivity at 1 and 10 min in the stress-test report). No coastline clipping (inland city, not needed).

robustness.basis: printed times; no alternative readings affect 08:00 (no historical buses: a lower bound)
